category_coverage.definition: number of distinct records that have at least one matched skill in the category; a record is counted at most once per category even when several of its matched skills belong to the same category

cooccurrence_matrix.diagonal: zero by definition — a skill never cooccurs with itself (no self-pairs); the matrix is symmetric and each cell counts distinct records

cooccurrence_pairs.definition: unordered pairs of distinct skills built from unique per-record skill sets; each pair is canonical (skill_a < skill_b), never reflexive, never duplicated in reverse order, and counted once per record

definitions.category_coverage: number of distinct records that have at least one matched skill in the category; a record is counted at most once per category even when several of its matched skills belong to the same category
definitions.cooccurrence_matrix: symmetric matrix over all taxonomy skill ids (sorted); cell [i][j] is the number of distinct records containing both skills; the diagonal is zero by definition (no self-pairs)
definitions.cooccurrence_pairs: unordered pairs of distinct skills built from unique per-record skill sets; each pair is canonical (skill_a < skill_b), never reflexive, never duplicated in reverse order, and counted once per record
definitions.skill_frequency: number of distinct records whose unique per-record skill set contains the skill; a skill counts at most once per record even when its terms occur many times in the record's text
definitions.zero_match_skills: taxonomy skills with zero matched records in the sample; a zero match is NOT evidence that jobs lack the skill, and it is distinct from no_evidence records (records where the taxonomy found no keyword at all)

guardrails: descriptive keyword evidence only: every metric is derived from the deterministic keyword baseline applied to the development sample; no embeddings, LLMs, semantic search, or fuzzy inference were used
not correlation: cooccurrence counts how often two skills appear in the same records; it does not measure any relationship, association, or dependency between skills
not causality: no metric here claims that one skill causes, predicts, or is required by another

not market coverage: the analysis covers exactly 20 records from one page (limit=20, offset=0) of one source (Himalayas), marked complete: false; it is not a market snapshot and no whole-market claim is made
not representative: this single-page sample of one job board is not representative of the Ecuadorian labor market or of any broader job market
no_evidence vs zero matches: no_evidence records are records where the taxonomy found no keyword at all; a taxonomy skill with zero matches in this sample is not evidence that jobs lack that skill
limitations: development_sample: only the records of one persisted page are included (limit=20, offset=0); this is a bounded capture, not a full feed
complete: false — the development-sample path always marks the sample incomplete: this is a bounded single-page capture, not a complete-feed snapshot, and this is not market coverage
matches are keyword evidence only; no_evidence means the taxonomy found no keyword in the searched fields, not that the skill is absent
raw fields and the snapshot/capture identity are retained unchanged; derived skill evidence is purely additive
